hints.content: To translate quadrilateral $ABCD$ by $5$ units to the right, we basically translate quadrilateral $ABCD$'s vertices and connect them.

For example, point $\blueD{B(-6,1)}$ is translated to $\greenD{(-1,1)}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at negative one, two, B at negative six, one, C at negative seven, negative two, and D at zero negative five. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves five units right from vertex B at one, one.

hints.content:
Doing this for all vertices and connecting them, we get the following mapping:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at negative one, two, B at negative six, one, C at negative seven, negative two, and D at zero negative five. A dashed line moves five units right from all vertices to make a congruent quadrilateral image with vertices at four, two, five, negative five, negative one, one, and negative two, negative two.

question.content:
**Draw the image of quadrilateral $ABCD$ under a translation by $5$ units to the right.**
